reason: This text (Genesis 22, the Akedah narrative) depicts Abraham as an unquestioned leader whose orders are immediately obeyed. The servants ('young men') remain obedient and compliant throughout—Abraham tells them to stay behind, and they do so without protest. Isaac follows his father trustingly, questioning only about the sacrificial lamb in innocent terms, not antagonistically. There is no depiction of conflict, resistance, or antagonism from any of the regular people toward Abraham as leader.
